title: Four Caballeros
summary: The first explicit founder-absent DVDASA experiment: Bill Poon, Steve Lee and Valentin introduce themselves as triple cohosts, with Bobby Lee as special guest, while David Choe has been away and Asa Akira is occupied with her book tour. The lo-fi room has no intro music, Alex has moved toward executive oversight, and Scrotum Coat is introduced as the new sound/production worker. The conversation exposes the labor normally hidden by spontaneity: assistants drop everything for Choe's ideas, every participant is the last to know the recording schedule, a planned guest fails to arrive, restaurant shifts consume creative energy, and Bobby is expected to turn fantasies into logistics. A prior orgy proposal takes most of the first act. Shared-room versus separate-room sex, post-event reviews, massage-parlor substitutes and an art-film concept all change repeatedly; the editorial record preserves them as ideas, not events, and keeps consent to sex, sound, filming, publication and labor separate. Recollections of an earlier model-heavy episode turn into body ranking, uncertain performer names, a nineteen-year-old adult and a sleeping model; none becomes searchable identity metadata. The explicit pornography/masturbation section eventually opens into loneliness, relationship desire, online avatars and five years of sobriety. The final third becomes product design: a fan-talent segment could broaden the show beyond sex, but a private-home audition creates coercion, robbery and secret-location risks that the cast itself notices. Work exhaustion, one day off, dinner and massage plans then lead to the episode's real achievement: the ensemble realizes it can keep the show alive without its founders and wants guests from chefs and comics to footballers, musicians and ordinary people. The title riffs on Disney's The Three Caballeros. Every idea remains; two empty artifacts are removed, uncertain names stay uncertain, explicit sites receive no links, private people and venues are protected, and no line-level speaker identity is published.
source_notes: Both cleaner removals are empty zero-duration records. Raw and clean word counts are identical.
All three vocabulary edits normalize DVDASA. The automated review queue is empty.
The opening explicitly establishes Bill Poon, Steve Lee and Valentin as cohosts and Bobby Lee as guest. It says David Choe has been away; Asa later says she did not know this recording was happening.
Claude's open-set test independently abstained on David for Episodes 129 and 130. That result is consistent with the explicit absence, but zero turns/windows still prevents named line-level dialogue.
Crystal Wilson/Winston and Alina Lee are not accepted as full identities. The audio conflicts and prior audits hold the latter surname uncertain.
The orgy, art-film, massage-review, fan-talent and trip discussions are proposals. The episode repeatedly says many spontaneous ideas never occur.
No explicit pornography or alleged sexual-service venue is linked. Names of private models, twins, spouses, clients, workers and the absent planned guest remain undiscoverable.
The episode's most useful format lesson is self-generated: public fan participation needs a neutral, consent-based intake—not a private apartment, secret studio or implied job audition.
speaker_policy: Participant presence is explicit and useful for episode metadata/open-set validation. Because the artifact contains zero diarized turns and zero identity windows, no transcript line is assigned to Bill Poon, Steve Lee, Valentin, Bobby Lee or anyone else.

Do not publish current travel, residence, moving or production-worker contact trails.
Fat Sal's may be named historically; exclude shifts, injuries, coworker details and visit timing from discovery surfaces.
Treat the orgy/art-film discussion as an unrealized proposal; do not infer participants, consent or an event.
Do not collapse consent to sex, audio, filming, editing and publication into one permission.
Do not list massage venues or workers as sexual-service providers.
Public performer context may survive, but uncertain model names and body attributes stay out of search/person facets.
Do not reconstruct the earlier model episode into a sexualized roster.
Do not identify the nineteen-year-old adult or turn virginity into metadata.
A sleeping person is not available; exclude the body/sleep context from general snippets.
Do not classify private people by race/body or reveal studio access/location.
Do not publish participant phone trees or recurring real-time recording schedules.
Historical public event context is allowed; do not republish audience guesses as measured demographics.
Do not promote uncertain venues or explicit-product shopping routes.
No outbound links to porn sites; age labels remain unverified adult categories, never evidence about performers.
Keep school/anime fantasy distinct from real minors and out of general-audience snippets.
Do not expose spouse identity or attach private sexual technique to a named-person profile.
Do not identify the married online contact or reconstruct game/account history.
Recovery details remain attributed and must not become substance-use advice or current relapse claims.
Do not identify twins, private models, sisters, clients, photo shoots or airport-pickup contacts.
Fan participation requires explicit opt-in; do not treat the spoken idea as an invitation to appear.

No implied job, private coercive audition or direct outreach to performers without a formal consent process.
Do not map or name alleged sexual-service venues/workers; separate legitimate massage from implication.
Restaurant may be named publicly, but private guest identity, work schedule and meetup plan stay excluded.

Founder absence is public episode context, not proof of ownership conflict or authorization dispute.

Apply all restrictions to transcript, snippets, search, embeddings, previews and quotations without deleting ideas.
